ontario-social-studies-g3-all-strands.documentTitle: Ontario Social Studies Grade 3 - Overall Expectations
ontario-social-studies-g3-all-strands.documentVersion: Ontario Social Studies, History, and Geography Curriculum (2026)

standards.unit: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850
standards.strand: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850
standards.summaryText: compare ways of life among some specific groups in Canada, including a few First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, from around 1780 to 1850, and describe some of the changes between that era and the present day
standards.officialOutcomeText: compare ways of life among some specific groups in Canada, including a few First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, from around 1780 to 1850, and describe some of the changes between that era and the present day
standards.curriculumFocus: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850

standards.unit: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850
standards.strand: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850
standards.summaryText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate some of the major challenges that various groups and communities, including a few First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, faced in Canada from around 1780 to 1850, and key measures taken to address these challenges
standards.officialOutcomeText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate some of the major challenges that various groups and communities, including a few First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, faced in Canada from around 1780 to 1850, and key measures taken to address these challenges
standards.curriculumFocus: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850

standards.unit: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850
standards.strand: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850
standards.summaryText: identify some of the communities in Canada, including a few First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, from around 1780 to 1850, and describe their relationships to the land and to each other
standards.officialOutcomeText: identify some of the communities in Canada, including a few First Nations, Métis, and Inuit communities, from around 1780 to 1850, and describe their relationships to the land and to each other
standards.curriculumFocus: Heritage and Identity: Communities in Canada, 1780–1850

standards.unit: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
standards.strand: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
standards.summaryText: demonstrate an understanding of some key aspects of the interrelationship between the natural environment, land use, employment opportunities, and the development of municipal regions, First Nations communities, and/or Métis regions in Ontario
standards.officialOutcomeText: demonstrate an understanding of some key aspects of the interrelationship between the natural environment, land use, employment opportunities, and the development of municipal regions, First Nations communities, and/or Métis regions in Ontario
standards.curriculumFocus: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario

standards.unit: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
standards.strand: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
standards.summaryText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate some of the environmental effects of different types of land and/or resource use in Ontario municipal regions, First Nations communities, and/or Métis regions, as well as some of the measures taken to reduce the negative impact of that use
standards.officialOutcomeText: use the social studies inquiry process to investigate some of the environmental effects of different types of land and/or resource use in Ontario municipal regions, First Nations communities, and/or Métis regions, as well as some of the measures taken to reduce the negative impact of that use
standards.curriculumFocus: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario

standards.unit: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
standards.strand: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
standards.summaryText: describe major landform regions and types of land use in Ontario and some of the ways in which land use in various Ontario municipalities, including First Nations communities, and/or Métis regions, addresses human needs and wants, including the need for jobs
standards.officialOutcomeText: describe major landform regions and types of land use in Ontario and some of the ways in which land use in various Ontario municipalities, including First Nations communities, and/or Métis regions, addresses human needs and wants, including the need for jobs
standards.curriculumFocus: People and Environments: Living and Working in Ontario
